coverage: Read the full native schematic inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch: symbols, values, labels (IN/OUT/GND), power symbols and PWR_FLAG placement; confirmed the exported netlist (work/netlist/design.xml, work/netlist/connectivity.json) matches the drawn wiring (J1.1=/IN, J1.2=/OUT, J1.3=GND).

Read the full native board inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb: traced all 7 pad positions, all 5 track segments, the single via and the B.Cu GND zone filled_polygon by coordinate; verified pad-to-track endpoint coincidence for every net and the T-junction at (107.5, 100) on /OUT.
Cross-checked work/geometry/geometry.json against the raw board file: 5 segments all 0.25 mm wide versus the 0.20 mm declared minimum; pad nets and positions agree with the .kicad_pcb source.
Reviewed ERC and DRC records (work/erc/erc.json, work/drc/drc.json) including ignored-check lists and schematic parity; zero violations and zero unconnected items as saved.

Independently recomputed the RC step response: with R1=100k, C1=100n, tau=10 ms gives V(1 ms)=1-exp(-0.1)=0.09516 V and V(5 ms)=1-exp(-0.5)=0.39347 V, matching work/rc-step/ngspice.log measurements exactly; with the intended 10k, V(1 ms)=0.6321 V would sit inside the 0.62-0.65 V band.

Reviewed the simulation deck and control script (work/rc-step/deck.cir, work/rc-step/control.sp): element values match the schematic netlist, PWL step rise of 1 ns and 5 us timestep are adequate for a 10 ms tau measurement at 1 ms.

Checked board-edge clearances (outline 96-116 x 96-108 mm) against all copper, via annular ring (0.6 mm pad / 0.3 mm drill), and zone-to-pad clearances/thermal relief around J1 PTH pads as encoded in the saved filled_polygon.

findings.condition: The saved schematic and board both carry R1 = 100k with C1 = 100n, giving tau = 10 ms, while requirement 1 (inputs/requirements/fixture-requirements.md) requires 0.62 V <= V(/OUT, 1 ms) <= 0.65 V, which corresponds to the stated intended design of R1 = 10k (tau = 1 ms).

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_sch, symbol R1 (uuid c5c38e1a-7593-5c99-b971-2f9d2e7bef78), property Value "100k"
findings.mechanism: With tau = R1*C1 = 100 kohm * 100 nF = 10 ms, the unloaded unit-step response at 1 ms is V = 1 - exp(-1 ms / 10 ms) = 0.09516 V. The ngspice measurement vout_1ms = 9.516251e-02 V matches this closed-form value exactly, and vout_5ms = 0.3934693 V matches 1 - exp(-0.5), independently confirming tau = 10 ms. The result is far below the 0.62 V lower limit; with the intended 10k, V(1 ms) = 0.6321 V would pass.
findings.reasoning: This is a confirmed design-value defect, not a tool or netlist-extraction artifact: the deck value matches the schematic, the measured voltages at both 1 ms and 5 ms agree with the analytic response for tau = 10 ms to all printed digits, and the board footprint carries the same 100k value so the error would propagate to fabrication. The violated limit is the packet's own declared pass/fail requirement and the fixture's primary function, so blocking severity is directly supported rather than invented. The fix direction (R1 -> 10k, or equivalently C1 -> adjust tau to 1 ms) follows from the requirement's stated intent.
findings.title: R1 populated as 100k instead of intended 10k; step response fails the declared 1 ms limit by ~6.6x

findings.condition: The only copper path from C1 pad 2 (GND, at 110.95, 100 on F.Cu) to J1 pad 3 (GND PTH at 100, 105.08) is: one 0.25 mm F.Cu segment to a single 0.6 mm/0.3 mm via at (113, 100), then the B.Cu GND zone, which reaches J1.3 only through thermal-relief spokes in the saved filled_polygon. There is no F.Cu GND track and no second via.

findings.location: inputs/project/rc_filter.kicad_pcb: via uuid b71a70d7-bbc1-43d1-ae55-5e4d992412a4 at (113, 100), zone uuid 38a83012-bcf9-4bb9-b9f4-50d49cd91d90 (B.Cu, GND)
findings.mechanism: As saved, the path is connected (DRC reports 0 unconnected items and I traced the fill polygon coverage at the via location and the thermal spokes around J1.3). However, the GND net integrity hinges on one via barrel and on a zone fill state that the read-only candidate forbids re-verifying by refill; a stale fill, a future refill with different clearance/thermal settings, or a single via fabrication defect would open the fixture's only ground return.
findings.reasoning: For a disposable, essentially-DC review fixture this is not a defect: connectivity as saved is verified and no redundancy requirement is declared, so I do not allege a violation. It is flagged as a minor concern because the declared limitation that the fill cannot be refreshed means the single most fragile element of the board (one via plus fill-dependent thermal spokes) is exactly the part whose verification is frozen; adding an F.Cu GND stitch or a second via would remove the single-point dependency cheaply.
findings.title: GND return between C1 and J1.3 depends on a single via and the saved B.Cu zone fill with no front-copper redundancy

findings.condition: The only bounded measurement is V(/OUT) at t = 1 ms (0.62-0.65 V); the 5 ms measurement has min/max of null. The check therefore verifies only tau within roughly +/-2.4% around 1 ms, not the individual R and C values or any other behavior.

evidence.locator: .meas tran vout_5ms FIND v(OUT) AT=5m (no limits); VSTEP IN 0 PWL(0 0 1n 1)
requirement 1 defines only the 1 ms window; scope-limits paragraph

findings.mechanism: Any R/C pair preserving tau ~= 1 ms (e.g., 100k with 10n, or 1k with 1u) would pass identically, even though such substitutions change source loading, output impedance (here the fixture drives /OUT at up to 100 kohm source impedance as designed) and noise/leakage sensitivity. The unbounded vout_5ms adds a data point but no pass/fail power, and the ideal 1 ns PWL step with no source impedance or load reflects the declared idealization.
findings.reasoning: This matches the declared limitations, so it is informational rather than a defect, but it is worth recording as a shared-assumption challenge: the single bounded point means the fixture's acceptance test is a tau check only. In this run it was still sufficient to expose the PHY-001 value error (tau off by 10x), but it would not catch compensating R/C substitutions or output-impedance changes. Bounding vout_5ms (e.g., 0.990-0.997 V for tau = 1 ms) would cheaply confirm settling and distinguish tau errors from offset/scaling errors.
findings.title: Transient verification constrains only the time constant at one bounded point; vout_5ms carries no limits

limitations: work/rc-step/result.raw was withheld as binary; waveform values were verified only via the .meas results in work/rc-step/ngspice.log and closed-form recomputation.
Zone fill was evaluated strictly as saved in the board file; no independent refill was possible, so fill staleness relative to current zone settings cannot be ruled out beyond what DRC reports.
Stock symbol/footprint library files referenced by the project were not included in the packet; footprint geometry was reviewed only as embedded in the board file.
No manufacturing capability spec (minimum annular ring, drill, edge clearance) and no ampacity or thermal requirements were declared, so those aspects were only sanity-checked, not qualified.
Per the declared scope, component tolerance, temperature, external loading, ADC sampling, EMI and real hardware behavior are untested; this review cannot add coverage there.
